description: mta_sts_fetcher.rs:32-34 rejects '://', '/', '@' in domain but not '#' (fragment), '[' (IPv6 brackets), '?' (query string), or '%' (percent-encoding). A domain containing '#' causes the fragment to silently elide the path component. A domain containing '[' could confuse URL authority parsing on some backends. The domain at this callsite comes from a DNS RCPT address that has already passed SMTP validation, making exploitation implausible in practice — but the comment says 'SSRF note' and the guard is presented as a security boundary, which it isn't. Fix by using a stricter allowlist (hostname chars only: [a-zA-Z0-9.-]) or add the missing chars to the reject list.
